title: LanguagePreference
description: How a person wants TEXT presented to them, stored on THEIR OWN vault (ACL = self), ONE envelope per person: the interface language, the language to translate other people's writing into, and whether to translate automatically. The three are independent — a reader may want a Russian interface and English translations. Any platform that shows text can read it to open in the right language instead of asking again on every device. ABSENCE IS NOT A VALUE: no envelope, or an absent field, means the person has never chosen, so a reader keeps its own default and must not treat it as 'off'. A value a reader cannot act on (a language it has no interface for) is ignored, never replaced by a default. If duplicates exist, the one with the latest updatedAt wins; writers update that one in place.

uiLang.description: Interface language, as an ISO 639-1 / BCP-47 tag (e.g. "en", "ru", "nl"). A platform without that language leaves its interface as it is.

readingLang.description: Language to render OTHER people's messages and posts in, as an ISO 639-1 / BCP-47 tag. Not limited to interface languages.

autoTranslate.description: Translate incoming text into readingLang without being asked. Absent = never chosen, not false.

updatedAt.description: When the preference last changed: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (what Meshenger writes); an ISO 8601 date-time is accepted by readers too.
